comment: The paint channels of a material's .aseprite file (pc/tools/paint_channels.py reads this; the Aseprite extension learns the layers from the bridge's greeting, so a new channel is a row here and nothing else). Rows are bottom to top above the reference layer. channel: the game's map name (RPC material map_set, <layer>/<key>/[@object/]<channel>.png); layer: the .aseprite layer; blank: the value of a map that is not painted (8-bit gray; what the game reads when there is none); encoding: gray (RGBA gray layers, luminance is the value); seed: where the export gets the game's current map (image: its file in the package's tex/ and seed/, plane: the colour plane of a packed image, none for a file of its own); presets: a preset's value of this channel (0..1 of the 8-bit range) can be painted with the Material layer's swatches; visible, opacity: how the layer is exported. Look values (how the game shades a channel) are not here: they are the lighting settings and the catalog.

channels.about: relief: 128 is flat, brighter is raised, darker is sunk
